angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 602,476 km at 75.00 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.3337 +/- 0.0117 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 75.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.866 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Krenn et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-421 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A.301K/abstract): 602,476 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.833 +/- 0.048 solar masses from Krenn et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-421 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A.301K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5291 +/- 64 K from Krenn et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-421 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A.301K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Krenn et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-421 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...686A.301K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-421.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.484, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
